newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Riot police break up clashes in Hong Kong village.
newsitem.headline: Riot police break up clashes in Hong Kong village.

text.p: Hong Kong riot police broke up clashes on Friday between hundreds of villagers and stallholders at a flea market, police and government radio said.
The violence flared when the villagers threw bottles and stones at the stallholders to force them to close the market in the village in the rural New Territories area, the radio said.

The Yuen Long villagers accused the stallholders of illegally occupying farmland and damaging the environment. The stallholders charged that the villagers were trying to extort protection money from them, a police spokesman said.
Police believed some of the troublemakers had links to triad crime gangs, but there were no arrests, the spokesman said.
Several hundred riot police brought the situation under control, dispersing both crowds, he said.

The stallholders used to sell their wares at a flea market at nearby Sek Kong on land belonging to the British military garrison. That marketplace was closed two weeks ago as part of the preparation for Britain's handing Hong Kong back to China in mid-1997.
